szoveg_eredeti:
Explainable Multimodal Artificial Intelligence Predicts Renal Sinus Fat Invasion in Kidney Cancer

A multicenter retrospective study evaluating 875 patients with clear cell renal cell carcinoma found that an integrated multimodal predictive system achieved higher numerical predictive performance for renal sinus fat invasion than individual clinical, radiomics, or deep learning models alone. When evaluated on two independent multicenter evaluation cohorts, the multimodal system reached area under the receiver operating characteristic curve values of 0.791 (95% CI: 0.7213–0.8607) in the first test set and 0.777 (95% CI: 0.6894–0.8655) in the second test set.

The study cohort comprised clear cell renal cell carcinoma cases collected across four independent medical institutions to support the development and validation of the multimodal predictive system. Researchers divided the total sample of 875 patients into a primary training set of 445 patients, an internal validation set of 111 patients, and two external multicenter evaluation sets containing 181 and 138 patients, respectively.

For the radiomics component, investigators extracted quantitative features from both the intratumoral region of interest and expanded tumor-plus-peritumoral regions of interest dilated by 1 mm, 3 mm, and 5 mm. After constructing and testing multiple machine learning classifiers, the peri-3 mm ExtraTrees model showed the strongest numerical performance among radiomics approaches, yielding area under the curve values of 0.753 (95% CI: 0.6741–0.8322) in the first test set and 0.751 (95% CI: 0.6610–0.8406) in the second test set.

In parallel, the researchers trained two-dimensional, 2.5-dimensional, and three-dimensional deep learning architectures based on the ResNet34 convolutional neural network framework. Among these configurations, the 2.5D-Peri-5 mm deep learning model exhibited the most consistent numerical discrimination across both evaluation cohorts, recording area under the curve values of 0.762 (95% CI: 0.6886–0.8360) in test set 1 and 0.774 (95% CI: 0.6828–0.8651) in test set 2.

A standalone clinical model developed from significant clinical variables yielded area under the curve values of 0.735 (95% CI: 0.6571–0.8121) and 0.736 (95% CI: 0.6499–0.8216) across the two multicenter test cohorts. To construct the final multimodal predictive system, the representative models from each separate modality were integrated using a support vector machine stacking ensemble strategy, while overall diagnostic performance was assessed through area under the curve, sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy metrics.

Model interpretability was evaluated using SHAP analysis, which demonstrated that features originating from the 2.5D-Peri-5 mm deep learning model contributed most significantly to the final prediction of renal sinus fat invasion. The study authors concluded that the multimodal predictive system may offer adjunctive quantitative information for preoperative risk stratification in patients with suspicious computed tomography findings, but emphasized that prospective evaluation against existing expert assessment is necessary before clinical adoption.

Subject of Research: Preoperative prediction of renal sinus fat invasion in clear cell renal cell carcinoma using an explainable multimodal artificial intelligence system

Article Title: An explainable AI system for preoperative prediction of renal sinus fat invasion in clear cell renal cell carcinoma: a multicenter study

Article References: Lv, D., Zhou, H., Wang, Q., Wang, Z., Li, J., Yao, X., Pang, L., Hu, J., Zhao, T., Gong, B., Qiao, Y., & Shuang, W. (2026). An explainable AI system for preoperative prediction of renal sinus fat invasion in clear cell renal cell carcinoma: a multicenter study. Cancer Imaging. https://doi.org/10.1186/s40644-026-01160-3

Keywords: clear cell renal cell carcinoma, renal sinus fat invasion, multimodal predictive system, radiomics, deep learning, ResNet34, ExtraTrees classifier, support vector machine, stacking ensemble learning, SHAP analysis, preoperative prediction, computed tomography, multicenter study, intratumoral ROI, peritumoral ROI, area under the curve, risk stratification
